notes.text:
# Q16 grouped Q8 scratch preparation

State: source preparation only. Not compiled, tested, benchmarked or adopted.
No repository source was changed. No runtime or numerical pass is claimed.

Control is the exact runtime src tree from
bf122fd00440366a704b81c36d4d7c8884384e2b. control-src.tar and
control-manifest.json preserve its archive and per-file SHA256 digests.
candidate starts from that same tree; only cpu_backend.hpp differs.

The algorithm is independently adapted from this project's own Q16 prototype
in docs/benchmarks/q8-integer-activation-20260919.json, patches.int16.
The original 5a9518c experiment changed only standalone matvec_q8_0. Current
eligible grouped projections bypass that entry point and call dot_row_impl
directly, so replaying the old patch would miss grouped Q/K/V and gate/up.
No mx-llama.cpp source was copied or used to implement this change.

## Candidate behavior

- Standalone nonempty Q8 matvec packs its activations once before existing row
  partitioning/dispatch. Empty output/block cases retain the original no-read
  behavior. Public dot_q8_0 is unchanged.
- Eligible grouped decode packs once only when a Q8 projection is present.
  All Q8 projections reuse those values/scales; F32 and Q4_K branches still
  read the original float input. Group eligibility and row partitions remain
  the same. Ineligible groups retain the existing sequential fallback.
- Backend-owned int16 values and float scales are resized before dispatch.
  Workers only read them. Existing synchronous completion protects reuse;
  concurrent/reentrant calls on one backend remain unsupported. No pool,
  completion, exception propagation, API, CLI or environment knob is added.
- Batched matrix kernels for nbatch > 1 are unchanged. This is not a claim
  that all prefill arithmetic is unchanged: its final vocabulary projection,
  one-token prefill and single-column tail calls use the same Q8 matvec path.
  Those paths must be witnessed and checked numerically too.

## Integer arithmetic and fallback

Each block has 32 activations. The finite absolute peak selects scale
peak/32767. Values are rounded to nearest and packed with signed saturation.
NaN/Inf input, a nonzero peak whose scale becomes zero, or a nonfinite inverse
rejects packing for the whole call. Zero blocks pack as zero. Half weight
scales still use the existing F16C/software-half helper, including signed and
subnormal scales. Original dot_row_impl is retained byte-for-byte.

Each integer lane combines four int8*int16 products. Even allowing saturated
-32768, the absolute sum is at most 4*128*32768 = 2^24. Intermediate int32
products/sums cannot overflow, and their conversion to float is exact.
Scaling and reduction are float operations and differ from the original
float-activation dot; this is a precision change, not a lossless candidate.

Beyond the archived prototype, a row falls back to the original float dot
when weight_scale*activation_scale is nonfinite, or becomes zero from two
nonzero factors. A nonfinite final Q16 dot also falls back. This avoids
substituting a new intermediate scale/reduction overflow for the float result.
These additional branches have unmeasured performance cost. A nonzero rounded
subnormal combined scale still has ordinary floating-point rounding error;
the candidate does not claim exact equality with the float path.

Packing allocation failure occurs before output writes/worker publication and
propagates normally. A failed partial pack is never consumed: all rows take
the existing float path. Future checks must include a successful reuse after
failed packing/allocation, so retained scratch cannot expose stale values.

## Deferred validation plan

Do not start until parent confirms other correctness/timing jobs are idle.

1. Build exact control and candidate on MSVC, then GCC; preserve commands,
   compiler versions, source manifests and executable hashes. Keep the
   instrumented activation witness separate from binaries used for timing.
2. Adapt the archived independent scalar pack/product oracle, preserved as
   archived-integer-core.cpp, to renamed q16_values_/q16_scales_ and helpers.
   Its scalar quantizer and signed product/reduction remain independent.
   Cover 1/3/7/32 blocks, uneven rows, unaligned input, 1/4/6 workers, zero and
   signed extremes including weight -128, all finite half scales, half
   subnormals, saturation boundaries and output sentinels. Compare fallback
   cases with the exact control, including NaN/Inf, tiny scales, combined
   scale overflow/underflow and nonfinite Q16 reduction. No test executed yet.
3. Group oracle: compare grouped output to separate candidate calls and the
   scalar integer oracle for Q8, and to exact control for F32/Q4_K. Include
   three Q8 projections, mixed Q8/F32/Q4_K at nin=256 with uneven rows above
   the six-worker threshold, no-Q8 groups, one/empty projection, batches > 1,
   small rows, changing worker counts and fallback followed by valid reuse.
   Native error/drain/reconfiguration tests must still pass.
4. Build a scratch-only witness copy with separate counters for grouped and
   standalone packing attempts/successes, integer rows and row fallbacks.
   Update row counters atomically or in distinct per-worker slots, read only
   after synchronous completion. Do not add counters to timing binaries.
   For a valid three-Q8 eligible group, require one successful pack and integer
   row count equal to the sum of projection rows; the matching separate calls
   require three packs. No-Q8 groups require zero attempts. Invalid activation
   groups require zero integer rows and exact float outputs.
5. Run instrumented pinned 0.6B and 8B Q8 models on a multi-token prefill then
   forced steps. Reset counters at phase boundaries. Require grouped integer
   activation during decode and standalone activation during decode and final
   prefill vocabulary projection. Add one-token prefill and a prompt whose
   ubatch tail is one token. Record actual counts, not assumptions from speed.
6. Validate unchanged frozen 0.6B and optional 8B HF gates on control/candidate
   with the same pinned models, exact token IDs and commands. Keep every
   failure; do not relax bounds after results. Record path-controlled NLL cost
   against current float and the scalar reconstructed-Q16 float control.
   Reuse the independent long HF history to measure all finite logit deltas;
   rank agreement alone does not bound numerical cost or prove losslessness.
7. Only after correctness checks, run a fixed interleaved current/candidate/mx
   timing plan with per-process warmup and no competing workloads. Keep
   original thread/ubatch/token/model conditions and all samples. Report
   prefill and decode separately, including candidate/control and external
   gaps. Old Q16 speedups must not be added to newer grouped/prefill results.

The new independent 8B HF gate closes an available-reference gap only.
Full-corpus, maximum-context, broader-platform and external performance
requirements remain separate. Adoption needs a measured, accepted precision
cost and performance result; this source preparation satisfies neither.

review: One pack before synchronous grouped dispatch; shared buffers read-only in workers.
Standalone path handles final prefill projection and one-token/tail calls too.
Four signed8x16 products per integer lane fit int32 and convert to float exactly; subsequent arithmetic is a precision change.
Extreme combined scale and nonfinite result fall back to original row; extra branch cost unmeasured.
remaining: Activation witnesses for grouped and standalone paths including final prefill projection.
Frozen HF gates, path-controlled and long-history cost evidence.
Isolated current/candidate/mx performance; no adoption without accepted results.

# Prepared commands - NOT EXECUTED

Run only after the parent releases the current Linux validation hold and
confirms the workstation is available. These are correctness and activation
checks, not performance measurements. No command below was executed during
preparation. Keep all generated objects, executables and logs in this scratch
directory. Capture compiler version, binary hashes, commands, exits and logs.

## Windows MSVC

Use an x64 MSVC Developer PowerShell so `cl.exe` and link libraries are set.
Run each command separately and stop on any nonzero exit.

```powershell
$study = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'llmx-q16-group-study'
Set-Location -LiteralPath $study
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path validation/bin -ErrorAction Stop
cl /nologo /std:c++17 /O2 /EHsc /W4 /arch:AVX2 /I candidate/src /Fe:validation/bin/q16-oracle.exe /Fo:validation/bin/q16-oracle.obj validation/q16_oracle.cpp
cl /nologo /std:c++17 /O2 /EHsc /W4 /arch:AVX2 /DQ16_WITNESS /I witness/src /Fe:validation/bin/q16-witness.exe /Fo:validation/bin/q16-witness.obj validation/q16_oracle.cpp
cl /nologo /std:c++17 /O2 /EHsc /W4 /arch:AVX2 /I witness/src /Fe:validation/bin/model-witness.exe /Fo:validation/bin/model-witness.obj validation/model_witness.cpp
./validation/bin/q16-oracle.exe
./validation/bin/q16-witness.exe
$small = 'C:/Users/Marko/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF/snapshots/23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf'
./validation/bin/model-witness.exe $small validation/tokens-247.txt
$large = 'C:/Users/Marko/.lmstudio/models/Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF/Qwen3-8B-Q8_0.gguf'
./validation/bin/model-witness.exe $large validation/tokens-247.txt
```

Before every executable invocation, check `Get-Process llmx -ErrorAction
SilentlyContinue` and coordinate all other benchmark/model processes with the
parent. Do not terminate user processes. Stop on contention; keep the same
owned handles if a run must be polled. Large model loading needs a separate RAM
availability check; the commands do not grant permission to overcommit memory.

## Linux GCC

After explicitly transferring this owned scratch tree to an approved path,
from that path, run commands individually and stop on errors. The model paths
must name the verified same GGUF assets on that host.

```sh
mkdir validation/bin
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -mavx2 -mfma -mf16c -pthread -I candidate/src validation/q16_oracle.cpp -o validation/bin/q16-oracle
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -mavx2 -mfma -mf16c -pthread -DQ16_WITNESS -I witness/src validation/q16_oracle.cpp -o validation/bin/q16-witness
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -mavx2 -mfma -mf16c -pthread -I witness/src validation/model_witness.cpp -o validation/bin/model-witness
./validation/bin/q16-oracle
./validation/bin/q16-witness
./validation/bin/model-witness /approved/path/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf validation/tokens-247.txt
./validation/bin/model-witness /approved/path/Qwen3-8B-Q8_0.gguf validation/tokens-247.txt
```

## Scope and expected assertions

The scalar oracle is adapted from llmx's own archived `integer-core.cpp`.
It independently derives per-block scales, nearest-even integers and signed
64-bit products, then recreates the documented eight-lane FMA/reduction order.
Integer row results must match exactly. An independently detected packing,
combined-scale or final-result failure instead compares with the archived
float control. NaN results compare by classification; finite values, signed
zero and infinities compare by bits. The half conversion helper remains shared
with llmx, so this is not an independent proof of that helper.

All-Q8 groups compare both to that scalar oracle and to separate candidate
calls. F32/Q4_K mixed branches and batches above one compare to the exact
control grouped call. The cases cross the six-worker row threshold, uneven
rows, zero rows, zero batch, small and empty groups, and threads 1/2/6. Scale
cases include signed zero, both signs of finite half extremes, NaN/Inf,
combined-scale overflow/underflow and nonfinite accumulated results. Partial
packing failures in the final activation block are followed by valid calls on
the same backend. Signed weight extremes and nearest-even ties have explicit
product checks. Software half conversion is also exercised.

The access-only headers expose private members for checking packing results.
The control class is moved to a test-only namespace to permit direct comparison
in one translation unit. Neither change alters the measured candidate tree.
Neither source is a production API proposal.

Witness counters use relaxed atomics for worker increments. Resets and reads
occur only before submission or after synchronous completion. Successful group
and standalone packs have separate counters. A row counts once as integer only
after a finite final result; a nonpacked row, invalid combined scale or
nonfinite integer result counts once as a float fallback. Counters cover Q8
single-column row calls only, not unchanged batched float kernels or F32/Q4_K.
An ineligible group routed through separate calls counts as standalone.

The explicit witness assertions require one pack/178 rows for an eligible
three-Q8 group, three packs/178 rows for separate calls, no integer rows after
failed packing, and successful reuse. Mixed groups count only their Q8 rows;
all-F32/Q4_K groups count nothing. A single-projection group routes to one
standalone pack. The witness build's global atomics add contention; do not use
it for any speed or overhead claim.

The model witness uses six workers, ubatch 128 and the pinned independent 8B
HF fixture's 247 token IDs (also valid Qwen3 tokenizer IDs for 0.6B). It resets
counters around each synchronous operation and asserts finite logits:

| Operation | Expected Q16 activation |
| --- | --- |
| 16-token prefill | Exactly one standalone final vocabulary pack; no grouped packs |
| Following decode step | Grouped and standalone packs/rows |
| Fresh one-token prefill | Grouped and standalone packs/rows |
| Fresh 129-token prefill at ubatch 128 | One-column tail grouped packs plus standalone packs |

These activation checks do not compare model outputs to HF and do not establish
acceptable numerical cost, losslessness, a performance improvement or parity.
Independent HF 0.6B/8B gates, path-controlled PPL, long logits, required suites
and quiet alternating control/candidate/mx timing remain separate later gates.
Timing must use the untouched `candidate/src`, never `witness/src` or the
access-only headers.

Known pinned GGUF SHA256 values for later asset verification:

- 0.6B: `9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031`
- 8B: `408b955510e196121c1c375201744783b5c9a43c7956d73fc78df54c66e883d6`
